analysis.title: Federal Support For Ring of Fire – The Weekly Blueprint
key_insights: Ottawa committed on October 21 to match Ontario's initial investment of up to $1B over three years in Ring of Fire road infrastructure, with coordinated permitting and a First Nations engagement group. CIBC says the commitment was largely expected but views the formal funding confirmation positively.
CIBC sees BDT as the clearest beneficiary because of its Marten Falls partnership. TIH and the engineering names are also likely beneficiaries.

BDT's Piinahzii LP partnership (announced in May) was expanded on August 31 to include construction of the Marten Falls Community Access Road. Neither announcement disclosed a contract value. Third-party listings put the road at ~$1.3B, and CIBC estimates BDT's portion at ~$600MM, which could show up in pending Q3 backlog.
CIBC says BDT has growth drivers beyond data centres. Its shares were seemingly caught up in the broader weakness across AI 'pick-and-shovel' names.

ATRL was involved in preparing the Webequie Supply Road environmental assessment/impact statement. CIBC sees engineering opportunities across environmental studies, geotechnical work, detailed design, construction oversight and eventual mine development.

TIH could see demand for earthmoving equipment, rentals, parts and services from road construction, with mine development (such as Wyloo's proposed Eagle's Nest) adding a longer-duration aftermarket opportunity. Development depends on road access.

Further approvals, financing and indigenous engagement are still required, and support differs among affected First Nations. The announcement does not say how federal funds will be split among projects.

Planned access network (Exhibit 1): Anaconda/Painter Lake roads (~97 km, opening Nov 2030), Marten Falls Community Access Road (~184 km, 35 bridge and culvert structures, opening Nov 2031), Northern Road Link (117-164 km, construction spring 2028, opening Nov 2031), Webequie Supply Road (~107 km, opening Nov 2030).
Coverage-list price moves for the week to October 23: WSP +10.6%, Stantec +1.7%, Bird Construction -10.4%, Aecon -8.2%, Badger -7.0%, TerraVest -6.2%, Toromont -6.1%, Finning -4.8%.
ATRL was selected as Project & Program Manager and Operations partner for TxDOT's Austin District Traffic Management Center, a two-year term with renewal options.
STN and GFT JV were awarded a US$249MM NAVFAC Northwest Architect-Engineer IDIQ contract over five years.
RBA launched 'Buy Now' and 'Make Offer' options across North America, adding more than 10,000 listings to rbauction.com. International rollout is to follow.

Dodge: US construction starts fell 1.5% M/M in September to a US$1.33T seasonally adjusted annual rate. Non-residential fell 6.3% M/M and commercial fell 18.4%, including declines in data centers. Institutional rose 16.3%. YTD starts are up 14.3% Y/Y.
The AIA/Deltek ABI fell to 44.7 in September from 47.2 in August, the largest decline since May. Firm backlogs averaged 6.2 months at end of Q3 versus 6.6 months at end of Q1.

Canada is advancing CANDU talks with Türkiye for its second nuclear plant. Prime Minister Carney says ATRL's CANDU has a 'good chance'. No contract has been awarded, and ATRL expects a technology selection decision in H1/27. CIBC views this positively for ATRL.
The Philippines targets 1.2 GW of nuclear capacity by 2032 and up to 4.8 GW by 2050.
Manheim mid-month October index is 207.4, up 0.7% M/M and 2.2% Y/Y. September was the first Y/Y decline of 2026.

ACT Research estimated September net trailer orders at 42,700 units, up 311% Y/Y. FTR estimated 43,059 units, up 385% Y/Y and 78% M/M, the strongest since December 2022. FTR warned the strength may be hard to sustain. CIBC still looks for a sustained rebound in tank trailer demand for TVK.

market_movers.rationale: BDT (Bird Construction) is seen as the clearest beneficiary of federal Ring of Fire road funding through its Marten Falls partnership. CIBC estimates ~$600MM of the ~$1.3B access road could land in BDT's pending Q3 backlog.
TIH (Toromont) could see demand for equipment, rentals, parts and services from road construction and eventual mining.

ATRL (AtkinsRéalis) was involved in the Webequie Supply Road environmental assessment. CIBC views the Türkiye CANDU commentary positively, and ATRL won the TxDOT Austin traffic management center contract.
STN (Stantec) is a likely engineering beneficiary of Ring of Fire development. It and GFT won a US$249MM NAVFAC Northwest contract.
WSP is a likely engineering beneficiary of Ring of Fire development. Shares rose 10.6% on the week to October 23.
RBA launched Buy Now and Make Offer options across North America, adding more than 10,000 listings.
TVK (TerraVest) remains tied to tank trailer demand. CIBC looks for a sustained meaningful rebound, and September US trailer orders surged.

sector_views.rationale: The multiyear Ring of Fire road and community infrastructure program improves funding visibility. BDT is the most directly positioned, with engineers also likely beneficiaries.
Road construction and eventual mining could drive equipment and aftermarket demand. US trailer orders surged in September but FTR warns the strength may not last.
September starts fell 1.5% M/M and the ABI dropped to 44.7. Institutional and nonbuilding activity offset weak commercial and single family activity.

earnings_insights: BDT: CIBC suspects its share of the ~$1.3B Marten Falls access road could be reflected in pending Q3 backlog, and estimates ~$600MM. This is a CIBC estimate, not a company disclosure.
ATRL buybacks: ~6.8MM shares YTD through October 23 (~4.2% of shares outstanding), per SEDI filings.
RBA buybacks: ~5.4MM shares YTD (~2.9% of shares outstanding). STN: ~3.4MM (~3.0%). FTT: ~1.4MM (~1.1%). TVK: ~0.3MM (~1.2%). BYD: ~0.2MM (~0.6%).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Institutional and nonbuilding gains partly offset weaker commercial and single family activity. YTD starts are up 14.3% Y/Y.
The largest decline in billings since May. Institutional and multifamily firms have seen declines for six and five consecutive months.
Higher wholesale used vehicle prices. September was the first Y/Y decline of 2026.

macro_indicators.indicator: US heavy-duty trailer net orders (ACT Research)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Fleets are securing equipment for the 2027 cycle and getting ahead of tariff-related price increases.
The strongest since December 2022. FTR warns it may be hard to sustain.

risk_factors: Further approvals, financing and indigenous engagement are still needed for Ring of Fire development, and support differs among First Nations.
Mine development depends on road access.
FTR warns the September trailer order surge may be hard to sustain given trade uncertainty, high equipment costs, competing fleet capital needs and possible supply chain constraints.
The Canadian CANDU bid for Türkiye is competitive and no contract has been awarded.
vol_and_positioning: Coverage-list buyback activity through October 23 (SEDI): ATRL ~4.2% of shares outstanding YTD, STN ~3.0%, RBA ~2.9%.
geopolitical: Canada-Türkiye talks on CANDU technology for Türkiye's second nuclear power plant, with a competitive technology selection process.
Federal and Ontario funding for Ring of Fire roads, with a First Nations engagement group and differing support among affected First Nations.
Trade uncertainty and tariff-associated price hikes cited as factors in US trailer orders.
